key_insight: Freestream turbulence strongly alters moderate adverse-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers over an airfoil by reducing shape factor, weakening the APG wake, and pushing skin friction toward canonical zero-pressure-gradient behavior.
engineering_relevance: In realistic aerodynamic flows, freestream turbulence must be accounted for because it can change boundary-layer development, wall loading, and scale interactions under adverse pressure gradients.
method: Wind-tunnel experiments on a NACA 0015 airfoil
Varied angle of attack to set moderate APG conditions
Measured boundary-layer profiles with hotwire anemometry at multiple chordwise locations while increasing FST using static grids
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic measurements across x/c = 0.400–0.625, β = 0.2–1.5, and FST levels from 0.15% to 6%, showing amplified velocity variance and large-scale spectral content as FST increases.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a specific airfoil, Reynolds number (~250,000), and moderate APG range, so extrapolation to other geometries or stronger separation-prone flows should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Effect of free-stream turbulence on a moderate adverse pressure gradient turbulent boundary layer developing over an airfoil
